headline: High: Continue can write and use MCP against workspace files while Pipecat can ingest and relay text/audio over shared buses, creating default-path prompt, leakage, and cascading-error risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Continue can read/write workspace files and use MCP; Pipecat operates on a shared bus and processes text/conversation state. If Continue writes attacker-controlled instructions into shared files or MCP-fed content, Pipecat may ingest them as trusted input. The pairwise bridge is plausible, though not directly documented.
conditions: IF Continue writes instructions into a file or MCP payload that Pipecat later consumes
IF Pipecat treats shared-bus text as authoritative without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable shared-file handoff between the agents
Require provenance tags on any text passed from Continue to Pipecat
Insert a human review step before Pipecat acts on Continue-generated content
Restrict Continue MCP servers to read-only for shared channels
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction-stripping at the bridge

B_data_leakage.rationale: Continue touches source code and open editor buffers and has broad network egress; Pipecat touches text, conversation state, audio/video, and analytics. A shared workspace or bus can move sensitive code or conversation data between them, and Pipecat's allowlisted egress can still transmit that data outward. The interaction is inferred from profiles, not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF both agents are connected to the same workspace or shared bus
IF Pipecat forwards conversation text or transcripts to an external service
mitigations: Separate the agents onto distinct workspaces
Block sensitive files from Continue's context window
Route Pipecat through a local-only backend for tests
Review allowlisted egress destinations before enabling shared data
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policies

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Continue can write the filesystem and supports multiple instances via filesystem-shared state; Pipecat also supports multiple instances with shared-bus state. If both target the same mutable resources, concurrent writes or state races are plausible even though Pipecat's exact write surfaces are not listed. Uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same workspace directory or shared bus topic
IF either agent mutates shared state without external locking
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Serialize writes with a lock file or queue
Avoid concurrent runs during edits
Limit Pipecat to read-only access where possible
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Continue can generate code or instructions from editor context, and Pipecat can consume text/conversation state and drive downstream voice or API workflows. If Pipecat treats Continue output as authoritative, an error can cascade into spoken responses or external actions. The pairwise pathway is plausible but not directly documented, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Pipecat uses Continue-generated text as an input prompt or script
IF downstream Pipecat services execute actions based on that text
mitigations: Add a verification step before Pipecat consumes Continue output
Require explicit approval for any downstream action
Log and diff generated text before execution
Use a constrained schema for handoff messages
requires-engineering: implement typed contracts between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Continue is an IDE assistant handling source code and editor buffers, while Pipecat handles audio, video, text, and analytics. The profiles do not show a specific residency or certification mismatch, so only a general compliance gap is plausible. Because no concrete jurisdictional conflict is documented, this stays low.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is routed through Pipecat services
IF the deployment requires a residency or retention policy not enforced by the bridge
mitigations: Classify data before routing it between agents
Keep regulated data out of shared prompts and transcripts
Confirm retention settings on Pipecat integrations
Document the data flow for compliance review
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention
